documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, now 65. Apologized for the missed April slot (calendar mix-up).
Oncology: gyn-onc every 3 months; last visit in April, told no sign of the cancer.
COPD: no exacerbations. Albuterol 2-3x/week. Inhalers covered after the PA in March.
Tobacco: daily, unchanged; still not ready.
Function: independent; no falls; PHQ-2 0; cognition screen normal.
Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (dermatitis).
Exam: lungs diminished at bases, no wheeze; heart RRR; no edema; gait steady.
Prevention: DXA now that she's 65; mammogram this summer; LDCT November; colonoscopy due next year. Fall vaccines at the October nurse visit.
Labs today. RTC fall or as needed.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Indication: Screening, postmenopausal woman age 65. Lumbar spine L1-L4 and bilateral proximal femur measured; all regions analyzable. T-scores at the lumbar spine, femoral neck and total hip are all within the normal range (above -1.0).

documents.title: Bone density
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Theresa, your bone density scan is normal for both the hips and the spine. No treatment needed. Keep up the walking.

documents.title: RE: Bone density

documents.body: Good news for once! Thank you.

reports.text: Bilateral CC and MLO with tomosynthesis, compared with 8/6/2024. Scattered fibroglandular densities. No suspicious mass, calcification or distortion.

conditions.label: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with acute exacerbation

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (40 mg) by mouth once daily for 5 days

documents.title: Emergency department note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
ED provider note, visit 9/29/2025, faxed to PCP 9/30.
65F with COPD, high-risk HPV, and vaginal SCC diagnosed 10/2023 s/p radiation, here with worsening shortness of breath over a couple of days, more than her baseline. Home meds: fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol PRN. Allergies: sulfa (rash), latex (contact dermatitis). Current smoker.
SpO2 91% RA on arrival. Albuterol/ipratropium nebulizer given; SpO2 95% RA afterward and breathing eased.
Impression: acute exacerbation of COPD.
Dispo: home on prednisone 40 mg daily x 5 days; continue home inhalers; PCP follow-up within a week. Before discharge she acknowledged her smoking has caused her problems but felt it was likely too late to stop now.

documents.title: Call after ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED fax received. Called pt: breathing better than yesterday, took the first two prednisone doses with breakfast as told, using albuterol every 4-6 hours today. No fever. Booked follow-up with PCP Monday 10/6 at 11:00. Told her to call or go back if she is getting worse before then.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED 9/29 for a COPD flare (short ED note received: SpO2 91% on arrival, 95% after a neb; sent home on prednisone 40 mg x 5 days). Finished the steroid on 10/3. Breathing is back to her normal now; walking around the house and to the car without trouble. Using maintenance inhalers daily.
Watched her use both inhalers: disk technique good; with the capsule device she was not breathing in hard enough to rattle the capsule, corrected and she repeated it well.
Exam: speaking full sentences, no distress. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. Heart RRR. No edema.
A/P
1. COPD exacerbation, resolved. Continue current inhalers. Written action plan reviewed: when to use albuterol more, when to call.
2. Tobacco: she told the ED it's too late to quit. We talked it through again - quitting still reduces flares. Offered varenicline or patches with quitline support; she declined both today. Remains contemplative.
3. Flu and COVID vaccines at the nurse visit later this month.
RTC in a few months.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu (first year eligible at 65) in L deltoid; 2025-26 COVID in R deltoid. Gloves latex-free. Breathing comfortable today, no recent illness. No reaction during 15 min wait.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
Indication: Annual lung screening, current smoker. Comparison: 11/19/2024.
Technique: Low-dose helical CT chest without contrast.
Findings: Stable mild centrilobular emphysema. No pulmonary nodules. Lungs otherwise clear; no effusion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Heart size normal. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.

documents.title: COPD follow-up (video)
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video from home (snow day), identity confirmed with birthdate.
No further flares since the fall. Rescue inhaler about twice weekly. Maintenance inhalers daily; capsule technique she says is better since we went over it.
Gyn-onc visit in January was fine by her account; they are spacing her visits to every six months now.
November LDCT negative.
Still smoking. Not interested in medications. Will raise again in May.
Plan: continue regimen; refills current; wellness visit in May with labs.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV plus COPD check.
COPD: one ED-treated flare last September, none since. Albuterol twice a week or so. Inhalers: fluticasone/salmeterol 250/50 BID, tiotropium 18 mcg daily, albuterol PRN - no changes.
Vaginal SCC (stage I, radiation completed 1/2024): gyn-onc now every six months; she reports no evidence of disease at the last visit.
Tobacco: daily smoker. Asked again; she says she thinks about it more since the ED trip but isn't ready. Offer stands.
Function: independent, no falls, PHQ-2 0, cognition screen normal. Health care proxy on file (sister).
Allergies: sulfa, latex.
Exam: no distress. Lungs diminished throughout, no wheeze or crackles. Heart RRR. Abdomen soft. No edema. Gait normal.
Prevention: colonoscopy due (2016 normal) - GI referral placed. Mammogram due August - ordered. LDCT again in November. DXA 2025 normal. Vaccines current; flu/COVID in the fall.
Labs today. Follow-up in about six months for COPD.

documents.title: Lab results from Tuesday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Good morning Theresa - blood counts, kidney and liver function, sugar and cholesterol all look normal. Nothing to change. The GI office should reach out to set up the colonoscopy; let us know if you haven't heard from them in a few weeks.

documents.title: Albuterol refill
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Electronic refill request from mail order for albuterol HFA. Last fill 2/2026, use consistent with her pattern. Refilled per protocol, 2 inhalers with 3 refills, PCP to co-sign.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology follow-up
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Surveillance visit 7/14/2026. Diagnosis: squamous cell carcinoma of the vagina, FIGO stage I, definitive radiation completed 1/2024. Allergies: sulfa, latex. Medications per patient: fluticasone/salmeterol, tiotropium, albuterol.
Exam today without evidence of recurrence. No evidence of disease.
Plan: continue surveillance every 6 months. Smoking cessation encouraged.
